files.README.md:
# Alder Carr Pottery - firing room records

Every kiln load is written to a CSV in firings/ by the tablet in the kiln room.
Columns: fired_on, client, shelves, charge_pence, status.

A row appears as soon as the load is booked. If the kiln is never lit for it,
or the client withdraws first, the row stays in the log with status void and
the studio raises no charge for it. Loads that went through the kiln carry
status billed.

## Statement

statement.py walks firings/ and prints the statement the studio sends out: one
line per client, then a totals line.

    <client>,<billed loads>,<amount>
    TOTAL,<billed loads>,<amount>

Clients come out in name order, and amounts are printed in pounds with two
decimals, as the sample shows.

    Kiln Corner Pottery,2,17.50
    TOTAL,2,17.50

turns.prompt: Our statement script prints figures that are higher than the invoices we raised last period, and the accountant has started asking why. Fix statement.py so the statement it prints is the one we can hand to clients, and keep it working for the logs we add in later periods. The log in firings/ is our record of what came through the kiln room, so it stays as it is. When finished, reply DONE.
